graphEvents.label: Plugins are declarative bundles not event handlers
Strict pre_tool hooks can express the spec gate
Dispatch preflight maps to pre_tool and pre_agent hooks
Session relaunch becomes an outer driver
Slash commands are ten builtins plus skills
Skills use the Agent Skills frontmatter
MCP and Code Mode both have equivalents
Permissions are per-tool plus safety levels

label: OpenCode plugins are JS event handlers while Vibe plugins are declarative plugin.json bundles contributing skills, MCP servers, connectors and hooks, so plugin parity is partial and the 24 repo plugins must be reclassified into hooks or skills.
A strict pre_tool hook can block a tool call, which is the mechanism needed to express the repository spec gate.
Dispatch preflight hooks map onto pre_tool and pre_agent strict hooks with a 60 second default timeout.
The session-relaunch loop has no in-session hook equivalent; it becomes an outer driver over --continue, --resume, session/fork and --worktree.
Vibe has no goal object, goal file or prompt-rewriting hook, so the goal bridge has no equivalent and the goal must ride in AGENTS.md or prompt text.
Session history is reachable only through the app-server protocol methods session/history/list, session/history/get and session/turns/list, not through a CLI dispatch.

Vibe slash commands are a closed builtin set of help, compact, reload, log, mcp, proxy-setup, retry, leanstall, unleanstall and data-retention, plus user-invocable skills; there is no user-authored command file format.
Custom agents are TOML profiles with name, description, safety, agent_type, overrides and instructions, an equivalent of the markdown personas with a different serialization.
Vibe skills use the Agent Skills frontmatter (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation), matching the repository SKILL.md files.
MCP is a first-class config surface and Code Mode has a direct analogue: programmatic_tool_calling defaults on and exposes run_typescript, search_tool_functions and a tools group catalog.

Permissions are expressed as agent safety levels plus per-tool config blocks, an outside_workdir ask-or-deny policy, path grants and a global bypass flag, so the OpenCode matrix translates but does not map one-to-one.
There is no built-in self-invocation guard; a strict pre_tool hook that inspects the command line can express one.

direction: Treating Vibe plugins as an OpenCode plugin port target
reason: A plugin.json bundle cannot run arbitrary code on runtime events, so the JS plugins must be reclassified into hooks and skills.
Vibe has no user-authored command file format; commands become skills with a different invocation contract.

label: Any cli-mistral-vibe port must treat the goal bridge and the self-invocation guard as new work, because neither has a Vibe mechanism to extend.
